world.setting: An English country house in the Surrey heat, then the retreat to Dunkirk and a London military hospital; told back from 1999 by the girl who caused it.

briony.name: Briony Tallis
briony.look: a thin, watchful thirteen-year-old English girl in a plain white summer dress, dark hair cut straight at the jaw, 1935

cecilia.name: Cecilia Tallis
cecilia.look: a bored, elegant young Englishwoman of twenty-three in a green silk evening dress, dark hair pinned up, a cigarette, 1935

robbie.name: Robbie Turner
robbie.look: a tall young Englishman in his early twenties, the housekeeper's son, shirtsleeves and braces in summer, later a private's battledress, 1935-1940

lola.name: Lola Quincey
lola.look: a fifteen-year-old English girl, coppery hair, an older girl's dress worn too deliberately, 1935

library.look: the dim Tallis library at dusk, tall shelves, one lamp

bedroom.look: Briony's tidy, over-ordered child's bedroom, models in rows

hospital.look: St Thomas's in London under wartime discipline, scrubbed floors, rows of beds

shore.look: the beach at Dunkirk, men and abandoned equipment to the waterline

objects.why: the letter Robbie sends by mistake, and later Briony's drafts - this book is made of documents
the Tallis household is the machine that convicts him
the retreat to Dunkirk is the second half's engine
the accusation, the police, the sentence
the fountain and the broken vase - the book's opening image and its recurring one

spine.claim: A thirteen-year-old novelist watches a scene at a fountain she has no vocabulary for.
Desire becomes legible to everyone except the child interpreting it.
Interpretation becomes an act of violence, and a class system supplies the verdict.
The cost is paid by the two people who never got to answer.
The novel admits it is the crime, and the atonement is the lie.
